methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-institutional (11 sites) retrospective analysis of prospectively collected longitudinal ctDNA data (1,578 samples from 190 patients, median 7 tests/patient over 24.6 months) using a clinically validated Signatera 16-plex tumor-informed assay. Cox regression with ctDNA status as time-varying covariate addresses guarantee-time bias, an important methodological strength. Multivariate analysis adjusts for stage, sex, and mitotic rate. Sensitivity analysis for lead time using last-positive definition addresses transient fluctuations. Stage-stratified subgroup analyses support robustness. Variable timing of postoperative blood draws (0-60.83 months for first draw) is a notable limitation acknowledged, limiting early MRD assessment.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort analysis with prospectively collected samples at 11 institutions, mirroring clinical practice - Oxford LoE 2b. Strong translational relevance because adjuvant immunotherapy (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) is now standard for stage IIB-III melanoma without clear selection biomarkers. This work provides real-world evidence for ctDNA-guided surveillance and early intervention ('treat-on-molecular recurrence'), directly informing ongoing biomarker-guided trial design. Strikingly high HR (40.63) for anytime ctDNA positivity makes clinical utility clear.

reporting_quality.justification: Ethics approval documented (Salus #20099-04 exempt research determination under 45 CFR 164.501; consent waiver under 45 CFR 46.116(d)). Declaration of Helsinki compliance stated. Signatera assay validated and described (WES-based personalized mPCR, 16 SNVs, ≥2 SNVs threshold for positive). Software versions reported (R v4.2.2, survminer v0.4.9, survival v3.2.13). Figures and supplementary figures referenced for transparency. Patient flow diagram (Fig 1) supports STROBE adherence though not explicitly claimed. Note that Natera Inc. processed samples and analyzed data, a potential conflict of interest not described in excerpts reviewed.

novelty_literature.justification: Extends prior ctDNA-in-melanoma literature (Lee et al. 2018 stage II/III digital PCR, Tan et al. 2019 amplicon NGS, Eroglu et al. 2023 stage III-IV Signatera) to the broader stage I-IIIB resected population with substantially larger cohort (n=190, 1,578 samples) and longitudinal analysis. Novel contribution is detailed characterization of real-world ctDNA-driven clinical management changes in 26/34 ctDNA-positive patients, including three 'treat-on-molecular recurrence' cases with durable disease-free outcomes. The strong multivariate HR (25.36 adjusted) establishing ctDNA as the dominant prognostic factor over stage is clinically impactful.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear, well-structured manuscript with logical flow from cohort description through RFS analyses to clinical management impact. Figures are informative (Sankey diagram for ctDNA dynamics, flow diagrams for management scenarios, stratified KM curves). Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings with prior literature and explicitly addresses limitations. Specific patient vignettes (MAA095, MAA007, MAA009, MAA133, MAA245) illustrate clinical utility concretely.

key_strengths: Large multi-institutional real-world cohort (190 patients, 1,578 samples, 11 sites, median 7 tests/patient over 24.6 months) enabling robust longitudinal ctDNA analysis
Strikingly high adjusted HR (25.36, 95% CI 9.16-70.3) for ctDNA positivity as the dominant prognostic factor in multivariate analysis including stage, sex, and mitotic rate
Time-varying covariate Cox modeling addresses guarantee-time bias, and sensitivity analysis for lead time definitions supports robustness

Detailed real-world clinical management impact analysis: 76.5% of ctDNA-positive patients had treatment changes, with 3 'treat-on-molecular recurrence' cases demonstrating potential early intervention benefit
Median lead time of 3.3 months (primary) / 2.1 months (sensitivity) between ctDNA detection and radiographic recurrence quantified
key_concerns: Retrospective real-world design with variable timing of postoperative blood draws (0-60.83 months for first draw) limits MRD-specific claims, as authors acknowledge
Selection bias inherent to clinically ordered ctDNA testing; no standardized protocol
Potential conflict of interest: Natera, Inc. (assay manufacturer) participated in data analysis; not addressed in reviewed text
Small event numbers in some subgroups (e.g., 33 total recurrences, 3 treat-on-molecular recurrence cases) limit generalization
Prospective biomarker-guided interventional trials required to establish causation between ctDNA-guided intervention and improved outcomes
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid large-cohort real-world ctDNA biomarker study in resected melanoma with strong statistical approach and clinically compelling prognostic findings, fitting Tier 2 (Clinical Cancer Research / JCO Precision Oncology-caliber) with minor revisions.
